TimePeriod: Wilderness and conquest era, c. 1400-1200 BC
Region: The hill country of Judah (Hebron, Debir, Anab) and, after the conquest, Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod
History: The Anakim descended from Anak (Numbers 13:33; Deuteronomy 9:2). The spies reported them as giants: 'we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight' (Numbers 13:33). Joshua cut them off from the hill country, leaving a remnant only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod (Joshua 11:21-22). Caleb drove out Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak, from Hebron (Joshua 15:13-14), and Judges 1:20 records Caleb's taking of Hebron from the three sons of Anak.
Culture: A tall, formidable hill people whose walled towns and stature terrified the spies. Their cities in the hill country were the strongholds Caleb claimed by faith.
Religion: No distinct Anakim religion is described; they belong to the Canaanite world whose idolatry Israel was told to reject.
BibleConnection: The Anakim are the giants of the spies' report and of Caleb's faith: the very people Israel feared became the inheritance of the one spy who trusted God.
KeyScriptures: Numbers 13:28; Numbers 13:33; Deuteronomy 9:2; Joshua 11:21-22; Joshua 15:13-14; Judges 1:20
RelatedEvents: The Twelve Spies and Israel's Unbelief
